name: rt-memory
note: Ray tracing's memory (the SDK's d3d12.cpp ReleaseRtTargets): its own targets, held after it was turned off, kept a 6 GB card near Windows' budget with the frame at 200% of 2560x1440, and turned on and off again frames slowed to 8 a second for good. Now, off for 2 s, they are given back, and made again when it is next on. On a card with ray tracing (DXR), with AMD FSR (ray tracing needs anti-aliasing) from CV_VENDOR_DIR: Lighting on, then off (given back, the game at 60 again), on (its guides made again, lit), off (given back again).

expect: found(log, r'ray tracing: guides made at 2560x1440')
found(log, r'ray tracing: bounce lighting drawn')

steps.note: off: its targets given back after 2 s
expect: found(log, r'ray tracing: off a while, its \d+ targets given back')

steps.note: on again: its targets made again
expect: found(log, r'ray tracing: guides made at 2560x1440')
found(log, r'ray tracing: off a while, its \d+ targets given back')
